phase-plan.purpose: Converge runtime resources and progression with the gameplay design by making mana the canonical runtime resource, aligning crystal-facing systems with that model, and closing summon/title/entity progression follow-through on top of the stabilized gameplay lane.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: mana naming/resource convergence across content contracts, generated artifacts, engine actions, status surfaces, KAPLAY HUD output, authored summon runtime follow-through, and planning/docs sync for the gameplay lane. Remaining out of scope: explicit title equip UX and the final entity/archetype/occupation progression cleanup after summon runtime lands.

file.description: Canonical config/resource fields should use mana naming instead of carrying energy-era labels.
The runtime should expose mana through status and spell execution, not legacy energy wording.
Rest/train formulas and result text should align to mana as the runtime resource.
Spell-availability checks and combat execution should use authored spell mana cost wording end to end.
Canonical authored formulas and semantic-runtime projection data should carry mana field names so codegen artifacts stay aligned.
Schema authority should define mana field names for formulas and semantic-runtime projection.
KAPLAY HUD should present mana as the live combat resource and stop showing energy-era labels.
Architecture docs should reflect mana as canonical, authored room-entry events as live, and the current gameplay workflow accurately.

task.description: Replace remaining energy naming in content contracts, codegen inputs, engine actions, status surfaces, and KAPLAY HUD/runtime text with canonical mana naming.
Verify mana/crystal presentation across room-loop HUD/status/forge/combat surfaces so the gameplay lane reads as one coherent resource model.
Continue spell-runtime progression cleanup by replacing the remaining summon/title persistence gaps that still keep authored spell progression from fully matching the design.
Finish the remaining entity/archetype/occupation progression follow-through so gameplay progression systems are consistently driven by the canonical content packs.

decision.summary: Mana is the canonical gameplay resource name across contracts, generated artifacts, runtime logic, and UI.
decision.impact: The gameplay design, content source, codegen outputs, and KAPLAY/docs-site surfaces now speak the same resource language, which removes an unnecessary translation layer from the active game lane.

decision.summary: Generated contract artifacts should be updated by patching source JSON/schema authority, then rebuilding, not by hand-editing generated TS/C++/C# files.
decision.impact: The canonical content pipeline stays reproducible for TypeScript, C++, and C# consumers instead of drifting between languages.
